flagged.comment: Easement line types are not adequately defined in the plan legend. Multiple distinct easement types are depicted on the plans (Drainage Easement, Wastewater Easement, Water Easement, Electric Easement, Telephone Easement, Sidewalk Easement) but the legend defines only a generic 'Easement' symbol with '-PUE-' linetype. Each easement type shown on the plans must have a distinct, defined linetype in the legend.

Multiple distinct easement types are shown on the site plan sheets (Drainage Easement, Wastewater Easement, Water Easement/Vault Easement, Sidewalk Easement, Public Utility Easement, Electric Easement), but the legend defines only a generic 'Easement' symbol (dashed line with PUE text). Each easement type shown on the plans must have its own defined linetype and symbol in the legend to clearly differentiate easement categories.

The legend defines general "Existing Easement" and "Easement (PUE)" symbols but does not explicitly define a specific linetype for drainage easements. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires distinct linetype definitions for drainage easements in the plan legend.

Right-of-Way boundary symbol is not included in the plan legend. UCM 2.5.1.E.9 requires that all boundary elements including ROW boundaries be defined in the plan legend with appropriate symbol and linetype designations. The legend must include a distinct ROW boundary symbol.

The Right-of-Way (ROW) boundary symbol is not included in the site plan legend. UCM 2.5.1.E.9 requires ROW dimensions and legend definitions on all Austin Water civil plan sheets. Add ROW boundary linetype and symbol to the legend.

Right-of-Way (ROW) boundary symbol is not included in the plan legend on Sheet 3. While the ROW is labeled as text ("Valley View Road 50' R.O.W.") on plan sheets, the ROW boundary linetype must be defined in the legend.

The Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Recorded Instrument 2010070731), a perpetual no-build easement covering 0.31 acres in the NE interior of Lot 1, is not depicted as delineated linework on any site plan sheets. This recorded easement must be shown with delineated boundaries on all applicable plan sheets per UCM 2.5.1.E.11 requirement to show all existing infrastructure within the Limits of Construction.
areas: Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan Sheet 5

flagged.comment: Neither the City of Austin 100-year floodplain boundary nor the FEMA floodplain boundary is depicted as delineated linework on any site plan sheet. Although the project location is outside the 100-year floodplain (FEMA Zone X per cover sheet), LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) explicitly requires every site plan—including those outside floodplain areas—to affirmatively show (a) the City of Austin 100-year floodplain and (b) the FEMA floodplain as distinct delineated boundaries with linework, not merely in the legend. Add both floodplain boundaries to the appropriate plan sheets with distinct, defined linetypes.

Drainage easements recorded on the Cortez Heights plat (Vol 64/13, C8-71-079) and Trico Subdivision plat (Vol 69/14, C8S-74-075) are not properly depicted with complete recording instrument numbers on the plan sheets. The 25' Drainage Easement and 7.5' PUE from Vol 64/13 and the 10' Drainage Easement from Vol 69/14 identified in the property records are not verified on the submitted site plan. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires all recorded drainage easements to be depicted as delineated linework.

Street address for each building structure is not shown on the Austin Water utility plan sheet. Buildings 1-8 are identified only by building number and unit numbers on Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan), but no street address is visible for any building. Per UCM 2.5.1.E.14, the street address for all structures must appear on the lot where the structures are located on Austin Water utility plan sheets.

Buildings are labeled with unit numbers only (e.g., 'Unit 101', 'Unit 102') on the site plan and addressing plan sheets. UCM 2.5.1.E.14 requires the street address for all existing and proposed structures to appear on the lot(s) where structures are located on Austin Water utility plan sheets. For this multi-family project with 39 units, each building footprint must be labeled with its assigned street address in the format: 3759 Valley View Road, Unit [number] (or equivalent format confirmed with Address Management Services).
areas: Site plan, addressing plan, and all applicable building footprints

flagged.comment: Street addresses are not labeled on building structures on the site plan or addressing plan. Only building numbers (Bldg. 1-8) and unit numbers (Unit 101-806) are shown. Per UCM 2.5.1.E.14, the street address for all structures must appear on the lot(s) where the structures are located on utility plan sheets.

The legend defines only the City of Austin 100-year floodplain ('100 yr' linetype) but does not separately define the FEMA floodplain linetype. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires both the City of Austin 100-year floodplain and the FEMA floodplain to be depicted with distinct, defined linetypes in the plan legend. Add FEMA floodplain symbol and linetype to the legend, clearly distinguished from the local 100-year floodplain.

Floodplain line types in the legend show only "100 yr" without distinction between City of Austin 100-year floodplain and FEMA floodplain. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires that the City of Austin 100-year floodplain and FEMA floodplain be shown separately on plan sheets with distinct linetypes defined in the legend.

Property boundary lines are shown on site plan, grading plan, ESC plan, utility plan, and addressing plan, but are absent from the landscape plan. Property boundaries must appear on all applicable civil plan sheets per UCM 2.5.1.E.9.

Property boundary bearings show inconsistencies across sheets: Sheet 9 shows N62°36'57"W, Sheet 8 shows N63°39'57"W, and Sheet 29 shows N63°36'57"W for nominally the same boundary segment. Verify that all property boundary dimensions and bearings match the recorded Mecey Subdivision plat (Vol. 73, Pg. 76) and resolve discrepancies with clarification notes or a revised survey.

Property boundary linetype is inconsistent across plan sheets. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts the property boundary as a heavy dash-dot line, while Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) depicts it as a solid line. Property boundary linework must use consistent symbology throughout all discipline sheets.

Building use or function (Multi-Family Residential) is not labeled directly on building footprints on the site plan. Use information appears only in data tables on the plan sheet, not as direct labels on structures. Per BCM 1.2.7, site plan must show building location and size with use identification.

Existing versus proposed status is not labeled consistently. Existing adjacent buildings are labeled "Existing Apartment Building," but proposed buildings (Bldg. 1-8) are not labeled "Proposed" - only identified by building numbers. UCM 2.5.1.E.11 requires consistent labeling of existing versus proposed improvements.

Unit types (Two-Bedroom and Three-Bedroom) are not labeled on the site plan for multi-family residential buildings. Only unit numbers (Unit 101-806) are shown; unit types are not identified on the plans. Per City of Austin Addressing Standards, unit types must be labeled on site plan for multi-family residential projects.
